text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I'm starting onboarding of gpt-neox-20b-qat into the hosted catalog. Need a quick sync on quantization readiness (AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8), the calibration data, and final accuracy tradeoff approval.

Maya: Thanks Alex. Can you drop the exact weights + tokenizer locations and the config diff? I want to run a couple local validation passes.

Alex: weights are at s3://redwood-models/neox-20b/releases/v2/checkpoint.pt and tokenizer model at s3://redwood-models/neox-20b/tokenizer/model.spm.
config diff is a small patch:
```
model: gpt-neox-20b-qat
seq_len: 2048 -> 4096 (we keep 4096 in serving config)
rotary: yes
vocab_size: 50288 (tk model uses spm)
```
Note tokenizer is SentencePiece with byte fallback — beware of tokenization mismatch vs our tokenizers.

Sam: Re: tokenizer — last time we saw <unk> spikes when sentencepiece model had unk fallback enabled. Suggest running the tokenization parity script: `tools/tokenizer_parity.py --ref tok-v2 --cand model.spm --sample 10k`.

Evan: For quantization experiments I ran AWQ (4-bit, group=128) and GPTQ (4-bit, block=128) on a snapshot. Quick summary:
- AWQ 4-bit g128: avg latency +12ms, perplexity delta +0.9 over fp16, anecdotal LLM-Adv match in most prompt sets.
- GPTQ 4-bit b128: avg latency +9ms, perplexity delta +1.6, more brittle on long-context completions
- FP8 (experimental): lower mem, but requires runtime support; quality comparable to AWQ in some cases but unstable on KV cache with long seqs.

Maya: Can you share the calibration set used? Need to re-run evals on our benchmark suites (chat-smoke, longform, codegen).

Evan: Calibration data is s3://redwood-datasets/quant-cal/neox-20b/cal-10k.jsonl — mixture of longform + code + chat. I also saved a trimmed 2k subset for quick runs: s3://redwood-datasets/quant-cal/neox-20b/cal-2k.jsonl.

Sam: Did you run our automated regressions? I care about Rouge-L on longform, pass@1 for code, and MMLU for knowledge.

Evan: Ran the auto-regressions in CI (see job quant/regress/neox-20b/v2). Results (AWQ 4-bit g128 vs fp16 baseline):
- MMLU: -0.5% absolute
- Rouge-L (longform): -0.8 absolute
- pass@1 (code subset): -0.4% absolute
These are within the 'acceptable' degradation window we discussed for cost savings (~1% abs).

Alex: Product / PM sign-off needed for the ~1% MMLU drop. @Maya @Sam can you +1 if you think AWQ 4-bit g128 is acceptable to promote to hosted?

Maya: I'm +1 for AWQ 4-bit g128 for hosted-tier-lowcost, but we should gate it behind canary rollout to 5% traffic and side-by-side A/B evals for 72h. Need monitor alerts on MMLU and hallucination signals.

Sam: +1 on the technical side. Suggest we keep GPTQ as fallback for latency-sensitive customers if AWQ introduces any instability. Also add a tokenizer parity check in the onboarding checklist.

Alex: Perfect. I'll update the onboarding PR with: weights path, tokenizer parity step, quant config: `{"method": "awq", "bits": 4, "group": 128}`, calibration path, and rollout plan (canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% with auto-rollback on metric regression).

deploy-bot: CI: quant/regress/neox-20b/v2 — PASSED (12/12). Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/quant/neox-20b/v2/reports/index.html

Evan: I'll also attach a small kaizen note about the FP8 runtime gaps — will open a follow-up issue to track kernel support before considering FP8 for general availability.

Alex: Thanks all. Action items: (1) Alex update PR with canary/rollback plan & config; (2) Maya run parity + product sign-off doc; (3) Sam add fallback config for GPTQ; (4) Evan open FP8 runtime issue. We'll reconvene async if any regressions show up during canary. :thumbsup:
